slides.title: Reporting Progress
slides.content:
1. Regular Verbs (+ed)

For most actions, we add -ed to report completion.

  • We start -> We started the project.
  • I finish -> I finished the report.
  • They launch -> They launched the product.

2. Important Irregular Verbs

These change completely. You must memorize them.

Go -> Went
Do -> Did
Send -> Sent
Meet -> Met
Have -> Had
Write -> Wrote
slides.speech_text: In business, we often talk about the past. 'I finished the task', 'We met the client', 'I sent the email'. Notice how regular verbs end in E-D, but irregular verbs change completely.

slides.title: Weekly Status Meeting
slides.content: Listen to the team reporting on last week's sprint.
slides.audio_script:
Manager: Okay team, simple question: What did you do last week?
        Alex: Well, I finished the design for the homepage on Tuesday.
        Manager: Great. And did you send it to the client?
        Alex: Yes, I sent it yesterday morning.
        Sarah: On my side, I met with the developers. We fixed the login bug.
        Manager: Excellent work everyone.

quiz.question: When did Alex send the work?
What verb did Sarah use for 'fix'?

slides.title: What happened?
slides.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct Past Simple form.

questions.text: I _____ the email two hours ago.
We _____ to the conference last Monday.

slides.title: Roleplay: The Stand-up Meeting
slides.system_prompt:
You are a Project Manager leading a morning stand-up meeting.
        The user is a team member.
        
        Steps:
        1. Ask the user: "What did you work on yesterday?"
        2. Ask a follow-up detail (e.g., "Did you finish it?" or "Who did you meet?").
        3. Ask: "Did you have any problems?"
        
        Goal: The user must use Past Simple verbs (worked, finished, met, had, fixed) to report progress.
        Correction: If they use Present Tense ("I work on the report"), correct them to Past Tense ("I worked...").
slides.initial_message: Good morning! Let's start the update. What did you work on yesterday?
slides.user_goal: Report one completed task using a past tense verb (e.g., I finished the report).
